Project Summary: Astronaut Health Monitoring System
Our project aims to develop a smart health monitoring software system for astronauts during space missions. The system will continuously monitor astronauts' vital health signs, including heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen levels, and blood pressure. It will analyze health data, detect unusual changes, and generate alerts if any health risk is identified.
The software will help astronauts and mission control teams monitor health conditions, identify potential medical problems at an early stage, and make timely decisions. Our goal is to improve astronaut safety, support better healthcare in space, and make long-duration space missions safer and more reliable.
details:
AstroCare – Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring System

AstroCare is a web-based health monitoring solution designed to support astronaut health and safety during space missions.

Space environments present several challenges to human health, including microgravity, isolation, and changes in physiological conditions. Monitoring astronauts' health is therefore essential, particularly during long-duration missions.

Our proposed system provides a centralized dashboard to monitor vital health indicators, including heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen levels, and blood pressure. It identifies unusual readings, generates alerts, and maintains health records to help mission medical teams review changes in astronauts' health conditions.

The application includes user login and registration pages, astronaut profiles, a health monitoring dashboard, health analytics, an alert center, and system settings.

Our initial prototype demonstrates the monitoring interface using simulated health readings and rule-based alerts. In future development, we aim to integrate wearable sensors, AI-based health analysis, and secure real-time communication.

Our ultimate goal is to support astronaut well-being and contribute to safer and more reliable human space exploration.
